content.value_statement: Inconsistent interface decisions slow teams and weaken accessibility. This skill provides token structures, React patterns, templates, and checklists for a scalable design system.
actual_capabilities: Structure primitive and semantic tokens for color, typography, spacing, radii, and shadows.
Define predictable React and TypeScript component APIs with variants, sizes, composition, and polymorphic rendering.
Apply light and dark themes through CSS variables, utility classes, or theme providers.
Plan WCAG 2.1 AA support for contrast, keyboard navigation, ARIA, and screen readers.
Document components with purpose, usage, props, variants, accessibility details, and examples.
Audit design-system coverage with the included implementation checklist.
limitations: Provides guidance and templates; it does not build, test, package, or deploy a component library.
Component examples assume React, TypeScript, utility classes, and an existing class-name helper.
Accessibility guidance does not replace browser, screen-reader, keyboard, or contrast testing.
Example tokens and palettes require adaptation to each product and brand.

use_cases.title: Establish Product Foundations
use_cases.description: Define shared visual tokens and component principles before designing a new application.

use_cases.title: Build Reusable Components
use_cases.description: Create typed React components with consistent variants, composition patterns, theming, and accessibility behavior.

use_cases.title: Audit System Coverage
use_cases.description: Review an existing library for missing tokens, components, documentation, testing, governance, and accessibility requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Design System
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a design-system foundation for [product]. Define principles, token categories, core components, and accessibility requirements. Explain each decision briefly.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new product.

prompt_templates.title: Define Design Tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Design primitive and semantic tokens for [brand]. Include color, typography, spacing, radii, shadows, and light and dark themes. Note accessibility constraints.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate token architecture for a product team.

prompt_templates.title: Specify a Component Family
prompt_templates.prompt: Specify the React and TypeScript architecture for [component family]. Cover APIs, variants, composition, states, keyboard behavior, ARIA, documentation, and tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced component planning for frontend implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a System Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [existing interface] against the included checklist. Prioritize gaps, map legacy styles to tokens, define deprecations, and propose a staged adoption plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration planning across several applications.

output_examples.input: Create foundations for a business dashboard with light and dark themes.
output: A token hierarchy covering brand, text, surfaces, feedback, typography, spacing, radii, and shadows.
Semantic light and dark theme mappings with contrast requirements.
A first component set covering buttons, inputs, navigation, tables, dialogs, and feedback.

output_examples.input: Review an existing React component library for accessibility and consistency.
output: A prioritized inventory of token, component, documentation, and governance gaps.
Accessibility findings covering contrast, keyboard support, focus management, semantics, and ARIA.
A staged remediation plan with migration and deprecation guidance.

output_examples.input: Define a reusable form component family.
output: Clear responsibilities for labels, inputs, hints, errors, and grouped controls.
Consistent properties for sizes, validation states, disabled behavior, and required fields.
Keyboard, screen-reader, documentation, and testing requirements for every component.

best_practices: Separate primitive values from semantic tokens so themes and brands can change without rewriting components.
Build accessibility into component APIs, examples, tests, and documentation from the first implementation.
Document migration, versioning, deprecation, and ownership rules before broad adoption.
anti_patterns: Do not expose raw palette values throughout product code when semantic tokens can express intent.
Do not create highly configurable components that replace clear composition with many unrelated properties.
Do not claim accessibility compliance without keyboard, screen-reader, contrast, and browser testing.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a complete component library?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture, templates, examples, and checklists that guide implementation.

faq.question: Which frontend stack do the examples use?
faq.answer: The component examples use React, TypeScript, and utility-style class names.

faq.question: Can it support dark mode?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers CSS variables, utility-class dark mode, theme providers, and semantic token mappings.

faq.question: Does it address accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers WCAG 2.1 AA contrast, keyboard navigation, focus management, ARIA, semantics, and screen-reader considerations.

faq.question: Can I use it with an existing design system?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the checklist to identify gaps, then adapt the token and component patterns incrementally.

faq.question: Does it include governance guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It discusses documentation, semantic versioning, deprecation, migration guides, adoption, feedback, and maintenance.
